steps: Start with an official blank workspace and no documents, assets or registrations. Create a definition, import one real synthesized PCM16 WAV through the visible media window, and ordinarily save its inserted reference.

Create one Scene2D, unchanged official checkpoint publisher and event-audio TXT scripts, two independent behavior-triggered tracks sharing the imported WAV, and a one-member project assembly entirely through ordinary controls.

Before first Save, reading and choosing saved audio declarations preserve raw JSON and approved review. Explicit Use writes the second music track identity into the chosen existing String parameter and revokes review; equal-value Use preserves it. Two held real HTTP requests cannot overwrite later input or another binding. Invalid JSON, three language layouts and Cancel preserve all author bytes.

Exactly one behavior.create apply saves both bindings with the selected second declared music track. Reload preserves the exact reviewed source. Retain seven documents, one actual WAV and a valid one-member project plan for independent native event/audio verification.

limitations: The harness initializes the official blank template layout with one generic document type and zero authored documents/assets/registrations. It does not automate desktop-library project creation, native folder pickers, installed Tauri or Android.

Seven documents (definition, one scene, two official TXT scripts, audio, assembly and first behavior) and one synthesized PCM16 WAV are created or imported through actual Studio controls; no prepared game source, scene UUID or author registration is injected.

First-creation audio choices come only from the real saved scene audio directory. Load/selection never changes JSON; explicit Use fresh-checks and inserts one existing String token. The selected track is the second declaration, not the resource UUID. No playback is performed by this helper.

The retained author-final workspace and frozen plan enable a separate actual Godot checkpoint/audio-command check. This browser report does not claim native playback, audible output or independent distribution.
